Check genes and remove genes that have mostly zero expression

```{python}
count = count.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

genes_all_zero = (count.sum(axis=1) == 0)

print(
    f"\nGenes with 0 counts across ALL samples: {genes_all_zero.sum()} "
    f"({genes_all_zero.sum() / count.shape[0] * 100:.1f}%)"
)
```

```{python}
genes_most_zero = (count == 0).sum(axis=1)/count.shape[1]
print(f"\nGenes with >90% zeros across samples: {(genes_most_zero >0.9).sum()}")
print(f"\nGenes with >50% zeros across samples: {(genes_most_zero>0.5).sum()}")
```

```{python}
#drop genes with zero 
count = count.loc[~genes_all_zero]
count.shape
```

we will filter low expression genes using CPM (Counts Per Million).

```{python}
sample["condition"] = sample["group"].str.contains(
    "control", case=False, na=False
).map({True: "Normal", False: "PCOS"})
```

```{python}
n_normal = sample["condition"].astype(str).str.contains(
    "Normal", case=False, na=False
).sum()

print(f"\nNumber of normal samples: {n_normal}")

 
# Step 1: convert raw counts to CPM
lib_sizes_for_cpm = count.sum(axis=0)                     # total counts per sample
cpm = count.div(lib_sizes_for_cpm, axis=1) * 1e6           # genes x samples, now in CPM
 
# Step 2: set thresholds
min_cpm = 1                                  # CPM threshold for "expressed" 1 or higher 
min_samples = max(10, n_normal // 2)         # tied to smaller group (half the normal)
#Use half of the normal samples, but never go below 10
 
# Step 3: apply filter on CPM values, but keep the ORIGINAL raw counts
# for DESeq2 -- CPM is only used here to decide which genes to keep,
# DESeq2 still needs untouched raw integer counts to run correctly.
keep = (cpm >= min_cpm).sum(axis=1) >= min_samples
count_filtered = count.loc[keep]
 
print(f"\nFiltering: keep genes with >= {min_cpm} CPM in >= {min_samples} samples")
print(f"Genes before filtering: {count.shape[0]}")
print(f"Genes after filtering:  {count_filtered.shape[0]}")
print(f"Genes removed:          {count.shape[0] - count_filtered.shape[0]}")
```

Perform PCA

```{python}
sample = sample.set_index("group")
```

```{python}
import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

log_counts = np.log2(count_filtered.T + 1)#compress values for analysis
 
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
coords = pca.fit_transform(log_counts)
 

plot_df = pd.DataFrame(coords, columns=["PC1", "PC2"], index=count_filtered.columns)
plot_df["sample_type"] = sample.loc[plot_df.index, "condition"].values
 
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 7))
sns.scatterplot(data=plot_df, x="PC1", y="PC2", hue="sample_type", s=15, alpha=0.6)
plt.title("PCA — PCOS vs. Normal (QC check)")
plt.xlabel(f"PC1 ({pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0]*100:.1f}%)")
plt.ylabel(f"PC2 ({pca.explained_variance_ratio_[1]*100:.1f}%)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```

```{python}
count_filtered.to_csv("count_filtered.csv")
sample.to_csv("sample.csv")
```
